'''''Cistus inflatus''''' is a [[shrub]]by [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Cistaceae]], often known as '''''Cistus psilosepalus''''', although this name is a [[Synonym (biology)|synonym]] of the hybrid ''Cistus'' × ''laxus''. It has white flowers.

==Description==
''Cistus inflatus'' is a slightly spreading shrub, up to {{convert|1|m|ft|abbr=on|0}} tall. It leaves are green, oblong in shape, usually {{convert|2|–|6|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} long by {{convert|5|–|20|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} wide, with turned under (revolute) margins, variably hairy, with long simple and stellate hairs on both sides. The leaves are unstalked (sessile) and, at least near the base, have three veins. The flowers are arranged in [[cyme (botany)|cyme]]s with one to five individual flowers, each {{convert|4|–|6|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} across with five white [[petal]]s with narrowed yellow bases, and five [[sepal]]s. The [[Style (botany)|style]] is very short.<ref name=Warb68/><ref name=LCVH/>

==Taxonomy==
''Cistus inflatus'' has a somewhat confused nomenclatural history. In 1786, [[Jean-Baptiste Lamarck]] described this species under the name ''Cistus hirsutus'', but it was an [[Nomen illegitimum|illegitimate name]] since he had earlier used it for a different species.<ref name=IPNI_77069425-1/><ref name=GRIN_402755/> In 1826, [[Robert Sweet (botanist)|Robert Sweet]] published the name ''Cistus psilosepalus'',<ref name=TPL_kew-2723599/> which was then applied to this species by many authors.<ref name=GRIN_402755/> In 1997, [[Jean-Pierre Demoly]] identified Sweet's [[Type (biology)|type]] as ''C.'' × ''laxus'' <small>Aiton</small>, a hybrid between this species and ''[[Cistus populifolius|C. populifolius]]''.<ref name=LCVH/><ref name=GRIN_402755/><ref name=Demo98/> As the name ''Cistus laxus'' was published by Aiton in 1789, it has priority over the name ''Cistus psilosepalus'', which becomes a [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]]. Demoly revived a name used (but not published) by [[Pierre André Pourret]], namely ''C. inflatus''.<ref name=Demo98/>

In summary, in Demoly's analysis:
* ''Cistus psilosepalus'' <small>Sweet</small> is a synonym of ''Cistus'' × ''laxus'' <small>Aiton</small>
* ''Cistus psilosepalus'' <small>auct., non Sweet</small> has incorrectly been used for what is now ''Cistus inflatus'' <small>Pourr. ex J.-P.Demoly</small>

Sweet called his ''C. psilosepalus'' "the smooth sepaled rock-rose" (the meaning of the epithet), describing it as "differing from all others ... by its smooth glossy sepals",<ref name=Swee26/> whereas later sources (including ''[[Flora Europaea]]'') described ''C. psilosepalus'' as having hairy sepals.<ref name=Warb68/> In ''C.'' × ''laxus'' the backs of the outer sepals are hairless (glabrous); in ''C.'' ''inflatus'' they are hairy.<ref name=LCVH/>

A 2011 [[Molecular phylogenetics|molecular phylogenetic study]] placed ''C. inflatus'' in the [[Cistus#Phylogeny|white and whitish pink clade]] of ''Cistus'' species. No particularly close relationship to any other species in the clade was identified.<ref name=CiveLeclDemoAgna11/>

==Phylogeny==
''Cistus inflatus'' belongs to the white and whitish pink flowered clade of ''Cistus'' species.

==Distribution==
''Cistus inflatus'' (generally recorded as ''C. psilosepalus'') is native to [[Portugal]], western [[Spain]], and two small regions of north-west [[France]].<ref name=Warb68/><ref name=eFlo/>
